caption: An observer watching the input cell fires 2 gt after each change of the input (both edges); inputs under 4 gt end while it is still busy with the first pulse.

An observer watching a redstone lamp lit by the input: the lamp lights at once and goes out 4 gt after the input falls, so the observer fires 2 gt after the rising edge and 6 gt after the falling one, even for a 1 gt input (min-pulse 1, where an observer watching the input needs 4).
An observer watching the input fires a 2 gt pulse 2 gt after each edge; the delay-2 repeater it feeds (on a stone block) stretches every pulse to 4 gt (4 gt more delay).
An observer watching the input fires a 2 gt pulse 2 gt after each edge; the delay-3 repeater it feeds (on a stone block) stretches every pulse to 6 gt (6 gt more delay).
An observer watching the input fires a 2 gt pulse 2 gt after each edge; the delay-4 repeater it feeds (on a stone block) stretches every pulse to 8 gt (8 gt more delay).
A repeater of delay 1 on a stone block: any input pulse shorter than its delay (2 gt) comes out stretched to 2 gt, 2 gt late; longer pulses pass unchanged (delay 2).
A repeater of delay 2 on a stone block: any input pulse shorter than its delay (4 gt) comes out stretched to 4 gt, 4 gt late; longer pulses pass unchanged.
A repeater of delay 3 on a stone block: any input pulse shorter than its delay (6 gt) comes out stretched to 6 gt, 6 gt late; longer pulses pass unchanged.
A repeater of delay 4 on a stone block: any input pulse shorter than its delay (8 gt) comes out stretched to 8 gt, 8 gt late; longer pulses pass unchanged.

An observer watching the input, a sticky piston under it (quasi-powered by the input, armed silently) and a sticky piston behind it (powered by the observer): the rising edge sets the pistons moving so the observer's first pulse misses the output cell; on the falling edge the observer fires in place into it (2 gt, 5 gt after the edge). Inputs of 4 gt or more.

A sticky piston (facing up) under an observer (facing up), the input beside the piston: every input pulse (4 gt or more) pushes the observer into the output cell, where it fires once for 2 gt; it is pulled back on the falling edge and fires out of the output's sight.

A sticky piston (facing up) under an observer (facing up); the input powers the piston and the output cell is where the observer lands: on the rising edge the observer is pushed into the output cell and fires 2 gt after it lands (2 gt pulse, 5 gt after the edge); on the falling edge it is pulled back and fires one cell lower, unseen by the output. Inputs of 4 gt or more.
